newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks close lower despite QNI merger.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks close lower despite QNI merger.

text.p: SPI Sycom 2682.0 -5.0 US 30yr cl 6.72 +0.03
10yrbond futs 92.890 -0.035 Gold NY 341.75 Lon fix 342.15
AUD US$0.7509 (Tues $0.7481) CRB Index cl 244.90 +1.37
*Stocks close lower after market meanders ahead of late QNI -Gencor nickel merger annoucement. Volume 444.4 million, value A$918.1 million, 1,206 traded, 360 steady, 378 up, 468 down
"Basically it seems as if things are going to be quiet for a while," Eyres Reed broker Martin Angel said.
"I think we're seeing a lot of book-squaring and tax-positioning."
Angel said the Australian market was also taking into account another possible cut in official interest rates.
The All Ordinaries defied the Dow Jones index on Tuesday to close over five points up but soon fell back into line with the U.S. market after a slight dip overnight on Wall Street.
"If Wall Street continues at around the same levels then our market will continue to factor in another rate cut," Angel said.

Other dealers had said earlier the market would only react to the anticipated QNI announcement if it involved a takeover by the South African mining house Gencor, with the probable result being the redirection of funds into other resource stocks.
The mining index barely moved after the late afternoon merger announcement and closed four points down at 946.3.
"People expected something different and the merger sort of took the shine off it," Angel said.
Shares in BHP, Australia's biggest listed company, sold fitfully throughout the day in what one Sydney-based dealer described as random trade.
BHP closed three cents down at A$19.70 after 4.7 million shares were traded, 1.5 million of them in a single parcel shortly after opening.
WMC fell back after gains on Tuesday to close 11 cents down at A$8.44 on trade of 3.9 million shares. Rio Tinto was up 3.5 cents to A$23.23 in similarly patchy trade.
Sensitivity to a possible interest rate cut saw bank stocks down after a strong start to the week but dealers said the banks were still among the best performers on the local bourse.
Banks helped the market to its previous records but both the banks and insurers' indices were down by almost one percent.
National Australia Bank fell 20 cents to A$18.65, Commonwealth Bank dropped 14 cents to A$15.05 and ANZ lost 15 cents to A$9.55.
"They might be down a little bit but the banks have been performing extremely well lately," a Sydney dealer said.

In other market news, Australian debt yields closed just above the seven percent barrier but traders said the move lacked conviction. At 4.35 p.m. (0635 GMT), the 10 year T-bond was down 0.040 points at 92.885.
The Australian dollar faded after making modest gains and was trading at US$0.7515/20 at 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT).
